title: Best AI subscription under $80/month for game dev
author: ktash8
selftext:
I have a budget of $80/month for an AI subscription, mainly for game development.

I'm considering Google AI Ultra, but I'm open to other options.

I work with C++, JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, Cocos2d-x, Cocos Creator, Phaser, PIxijs and other game development technologies. My experience also includes HTML5 game development, backend architecture, multiplayer systems, game server development, API integration, debugging, and working with large existing codebases.

Which AI subscription would give me the best value for coding, debugging, understanding large codebases, and building games? What would you recommend? I'd love to hear real world experiences!

comments.author: OneMoreFightGame
comments.body: I'm fairly new to this, and it's not under $80, but for $20 more per month Claude has been fantastic for me

replies.author: ktash8
replies.body: Claude's $20 plan runs out of usage limits very quickly. I m experiencing something similar with Google Gemini Pro. The usage lasts longer, but there's a limit on access to the higher end models. That's why I'm asking this question.

replies.author: NagatoKami
replies.body: It runs out quickly because you let it. Adding skills and making a global contract puts a stop on the whole gaslighting thing. For once you pick the most capable model (for example Fable 5.2) and let it write rules, you apply those rules to it and then let it reiterate and fix loopholes (you can tell it, you analyze the contract with other agents which way you keep it in check). Once done you set the rules globally and use the lower models (Opus, Sonnet, etc). Without rules you are dealing with a bot which picks the path of least resistance and throws at you whatever sticks.

replies.author: ZeroZelath
replies.body: How do you setup these skills / rules?

replies.author: NagatoKami
replies.body:
You can write them in [skills.md](http://skills.md) file or look in the internet for github repos (copy the link and drop the link in the chat and tell the agent to install it and then you may need to type /whateverTheSkillNameIs to activate it. If you use a harness (Claude Code, Codex, whatever), they create a folder, drop the [rules.md](http://rules.md) in the chat and tell the agent to set it globally or only for the project if you want and it will write in it's folder.

For example drop this one which saves some tokens (https://github.com/juliusbrussee/caveman) to the agent and tell it to set it.

Edit: Don't just drop whatever you find, let the agent first check the repo/code/text is secure.

comments.author: ConclusionOk4815
comments.body:
I would say ChatGPT Pro at the $100 plan. I know its over your $80 budget, but to get the top models most plans start at the $100 range. While Claude is generally much easier to work with, I find ChatGPT to be just as capable, but requiring a bit more orchestration work on your end. The usage you get is unparalled in my opinion. I have a few large projects I am working on, and with pretty heavy usage, solely (no pun intended), on Astra, I never run out. They are also very generous about usage resets.

Gemini is another good option, but the usage is not as much, and there seems to be a significant veriance in the quality of gemini model outputs. Sometimes they are excellent and unique from what Claude or ChatGPT might come up with, but other times, they will nuke your codebase with the stupidest of mistkaes, which, with the current iteration of models, is something I have never experiences with Claude or ChatGPT.

In terms of creating games, ChatGPT computer use is unparalleled, and Astra 6.2 is much better at 3d modeling and understanding 3d worlds than its predeseccor.  I would asume this skill extends to their cheaper 6.2 Sol model. Additionally, if you are a developer who has a specific game in mind, and not "Chat, build GTA 7, make no mistakes", ChatGPT is very good at following your exact instructions, even to the projects detriment. Claude tends to guide you to its own ideas, for better or for worse.

Regardless, I would say that it is worth spending extra to get on a $100 plan with either Claude or ChatGPT, as the quality of models below the fronier drops off rapidly., to the point where they are simply not worth using for complex tasks.
